To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) our end-to-end system achieved the best overall performance in TempEval 2016; (2) the best performance of our system for all sub-tasks was achieved when plain texts were used as inputs; and (3) the best performance for narrative container relation extraction was obtained when gold standard annotations for event and time spans were given as inputs.

(1) a system that combines a rule-based system and machine learning models can outperform systems that use machine learning models only; and (2) a system can perform better when gold standard annotations are available.

(i) the best performance can be achieved by combining a state-of-the-art neural network-based system for event and time expression extraction with an existing rule-based system for temporal relation identification and (ii) a simple approach that uses gold standard event and time expression annotations for temporal relation identification can achieve comparable or even better results than the existing rule-based systems.
